request.deadline: 18-month transition and operations period, with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Not-for-profit entity established or host-organization agreement signed under a preliminary board in Q3 2026
Technical transition architecture and migration plan published for community review
Board election held via on-chain voting by Q4 2026 and elected board seated
Public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod served by the new stack by Q1 2027
Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets legally transferred to the governing entity
Public API operated at minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA with quarterly technical and budget reports
Sustainability consultation and proposal published in Q2-Q3 2027
request.recipient: Input Output / Blockfrost transition administered through Intersect and CDH contractual arrangements
request.what: Transition Blockfrost into a free, community-governed public good under an independent not-for-profit, including 18 months of transition and operations funding.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is described as a hosted REST interface that lets developers read from and interact with Cardano without running their own node infrastructure.
The proposal says Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem surveys show Blockfrost hosted-platform usage rose from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025.
The proposal states that in the previous month Blockfrost served 781,000 unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data.
The proposal states that more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost in most Cardano epochs.
The proposal states that more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the effort to decentralize Blockfrost operations.

The proposal states that 90% of all Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier, making the current commercial model challenging for financing the public-good operation.
The proposal commits to transferring Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the governing not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.
The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA, valued as 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, with 79.1% allocated to staffing, 19.3% to operations and infrastructure, and 1.6% to legal and accounting.
The proposal says unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury and quarterly reports will include technical data and a budget summary.
The proposal says milestone acceptance will be supported by a third-party assurer and project progress will be monitored through Intersect's delivery assurance function.

summary: The document presents a large treasury request to convert Blockfrost from a commercial service into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, with strong claimed ecosystem dependence but several key usage, cost, and sustainability claims stated without embedded independent evidence.
